toegepas.rede_vinder: 'Word welkom' (become welcome) is unidiomatic; 'word verwelkom' is the natural passive for being welcomed.
toegepas.fout: 'word welkom' (become welcome) is a stiff, unidiomatic construction for being received as welcome
toegepas.rede_keurder: 'Word verwelkom' is the natural Afrikaans passive, keeps the protected word 'vreemdelinge' and says the same thing.

toegepas.voor: Ons noem die gewoonte om nuwelinge ten volle op te neem heelhartige aanvaarding.
toegepas.na: Die gewoonte om nuwelinge ten volle op te neem, noem ons heelhartige aanvaarding.
toegepas.rede_vinder: The long om-te clause runs straight into the term, so a learner struggles to see where the name begins; fronting the clause with a comma makes the term stand clearly at the end.
toegepas.fout: the long om-te clause runs into the term with no break, so a Grade 5 reader cannot see where the name begins
toegepas.rede_keurder: Fronting the clause with a comma makes the term stand clearly at the end without changing the meaning or adding anything.

laat_vaar.blok: Grond vir die gesin en die vee
laat_vaar.rede_vinder: 'Van ... weet ons' is the natural way to say what is known about a group; 'uit' reads as coming out of the communities. The protected phrase stays intact.
laat_vaar.rede_keurder: 'Uit' marks later communities as the evidence the knowledge comes from, while 'van' reads as knowledge about them, so the preposition swap moves the deliberately limited claim and the original is good Afrikaans.

laat_vaar.voor: Taal is self 'n bron wat kontak wys.
laat_vaar.na: Taal self is 'n bron wat kontak wys.
laat_vaar.rede_vinder: Placing 'self' directly after 'Taal' gives the intended emphasis (language itself) more clearly than after the verb.
laat_vaar.rede_keurder: 'Taal is self 'n bron' already reads naturally as 'language is itself a source'; moving 'self' is a lateral move.

laat_vaar_vorige.na: dorpies waar mense lank gebly het.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_vinder: The rest of the sentence is in the past tense; the apposition should match.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_keurder: The apposition glosses the term 'gevestigde nedersettings' in general, so the present tense is right and the past narrows it to these villages.

laat_vaar_vorige.voor: Ons weet nie seker of die eerste boere ook so gemaak het nie.
laat_vaar_vorige.na: Ons weet nie seker of die eerste boere dit ook so gedoen het nie.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_vinder: 'so gemaak' is colloquial; 'dit so gedoen' is the clearer written form.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_keurder: 'so gemaak' is natural plain Afrikaans, and the proposal is only a different, slightly longer wording.

laat_vaar_vorige.voor: deur oorblyfsels te ondersoek wat mense agtergelaat het.
laat_vaar_vorige.na: deur oorblyfsels wat mense agtergelaat het, te ondersoek.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_vinder: The relative clause is split from its noun 'oorblyfsels'; keeping them together reads more naturally.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_keurder: Placing the relative clause after the verb is normal Afrikaans, and the proposal is harder for a Grade 5 reader and rewords a glossary definition.

laat_vaar_vorige.rede_vinder: 'hulle' can be read as the strangers' communities, and it repeats 'gemeenskappe' from earlier in the same sentence.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_keurder: 'hulle' reads naturally as the leaders' communities (the strangers cannot be taken into their own), and the singular 'die gemeenskap' after plural 'Leiers' is a lateral move with a slight number mismatch rather than a clear improvement.
